tom-finance: Heads-up: EU public sector customer (Municipality of Lulee5, SE) submitted invoice dispute. They say public bodies are VAT-exempt and want VAT refunded on prior invoices where we charged 25%. They applied promo credits too. Question: what documentary proof do we need and can we reissue?

sophie-tax: Good question. Public bodies can be exempt for certain supplies, but it depends on the nature of the service. For SaaS/API access, many EU countries treat it as taxable. Sweden: municipal bodies are typically taxable for commercial activities; however if they act under statute performing public functions, they may be exempt. We need an exemption certificate or legal basis from the customer + period of supply.

ella-cs: Customer says they purchased telematics API used for public transportation scheduling; they claim supplies are public services and exempt. They uploaded a Swedish tax authority letter and a municipal certification.

acct-pay: Practical: to process a refund/reissue we need: (1) original invoice numbers, (2) customer's exemption doc, (3) statement of supply dates, (4) whether the service was used for exempt function. We'll also need tax team approval and note code for the credit note.

ledger-bot: Invoices in question: INV-2025-2044 and INV-2025-2088. Links: https://billing.redwood/invoices/INV-2025-2044 , https://billing.redwood/invoices/INV-2025-2088

sophie-tax: Next steps from tax: 1) Review uploaded docs and confirm authority/date stamps. 2) Ask customer to fill a simple attestation: "Services purchased were for statutory public functions and are VAT-exempt under [citation]." 3) If exemption valid for the invoice periods, issue credit notes and reissue invoices net of VAT with narrative: "VAT exempt customer provided statutory exemption certificate" and attach scanned docs. 4) Keep audit trail in ticket FIN-6451.

tom-finance: OK. What about the promo credits? They reduced net before VAT. If we reissue net of VAT, do promo credits remain applied?

sophie-tax: Promo credits are discounts reducing taxable base. If original invoice had promo credits and VAT charged, and we reissue without VAT, credit notes should reflect same promo lines. Essentially: credit full original invoice then reissue composed of same net amounts but VAT 0.00. Add note: "promo credits applied: internal ref XPR-90".

ella-cs: Customer prefers reissue instead of refund. They want corrected invoices for their accounting.

legal-bot: Reminder: if we accept exemption, ensure contract/country law check completed. Also require a signed customer attestation to reduce dispute risk. Update SOW if recurring.

acct-pay: I'll prepare a template email and credit-note draft. Need tax to confirm exact wording for audit. Ticket FIN-6451 opened.

ledger-bot: Created draft credit notes CR-2026-1001 and CR-2026-1002 in draft folder.

acct-pay: Template draft:

"We have credited VAT charged on invoices INV-2025-2044 and INV-2025-2088 following receipt of municipal statutory exemption documentation. New invoices will be issued net of VAT. Please confirm the attestation and sign the attached confirmation."

sophie-tax: Wording ok. For the invoice narrative use: "VAT exempt under [statute reference]  customer attestation on file" and include the uploaded Swedish tax authority letter filename. Also include who reviewed it (sophie-tax) and date.

tom-finance: I'll send the template and ask customer to sign attestation. Also adding a product note to block 'auto-apply VAT' for accounts with approved exemption in billing metadata. Engineering/DevX please note.

ella-cs: Sent to customer. They signed attestation and returned it this morning. Docs attached to FIN-6451.

acct-pay: With signed attestation and documents, we're clear to reissue. Will process credit notes and new invoices next payment window.

ledger-bot: Credit notes issued CR-2026-1001 and CR-2026-1002. New invoices reissued INV-2026-3001 and INV-2026-3002 (VAT 0.00). Links provided in ticket FIN-6451.

tom-finance: Thanks everyone. Closing once refunds/adjustments are reconciled in ledger. Also let's add an internal doc on public-sector exemption handling (SOP). :memo:
